svg.title: Japan at a glance
svg.desc: Static vector infographic about Japan: a stylised prefecture map with Tokyo, Yokohama, Nagoya and Osaka; a bar chart of nominal GDP in current US dollars for 2015-2024; a donut chart of population composition by nationality; and six destinations to visit.
svg.text: An island nation of 124 million people, 14,125 islands and the world's second-largest economy
Four main islands and a long tail of smaller ones
The land, the people, the scale
Japan is an archipelago of 14,125 islands in the northwest
Pacific, strung out along a mountain spine that runs some
3,000 kilometres from Hokkaido to Kyushu. Three quarters
of its people live on four islands, and almost all of them
in cities hugging the narrow coastal plain.
Japan is an archipelago of 14,125 islands in the northwest Pacific, stretching some 3,000 kilometres from end to
end. Three quarters of its people live on the four main islands — and almost all of them in cities that climb
hillsides, on farms that terrace mountainsides, linked by bullet trains that cross the archipelago in under three
Japan's nominal GDP peaked at $5.12 trillion in
2019 and has retreated by more than a fifth
since, as the yen sagged against the dollar and
terms it is still the second-largest economy on
Japan's economy in trillions of current US dollars
Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators · 2024 figure preliminary
The remaining 2.5% of the population, enlarged for clarity
Six places that explain the country
Neon, shrines and the world's biggest food market
Japan's kitchen: street food and Osaka Castle
A city of memory and its shrine on the water
The sacred peak, onsen towns and lake views
Powder snow, summer lavender and open roads
Sources: World Bank, World Development Indicators (GDP, current US$); Government of Japan, Ministry of Justice — Register of Foreigners (population composition);
Statistics Bureau of Japan; CIA World Factbook (area). GDP 2024 preliminary. Map and charts are stylised for design; figures are rounded.
